pr.title: List only the session's own loops in Projector's band
pr.head: 5c1e14297ae55274af1440d744c5a9639d4b9024

summary: Projector's band is the strip above the Claude Code prompt that the plugin's hooks module (hooks/register.tsx) draws. It lists, one line each, the open pull requests that the session's loops track. A loop is a start-review-loop or start-fix-loop run, and its watcher script (watch-prs.sh or watch-threads.sh) reads a tracked file that names one pull request per line.

Before this change, the band also ran ps on every reload and adopted every watcher running anywhere on the machine. A session that started no loop of its own therefore listed another session's pull requests, sometimes dozens of them. The band now lists only the session's own loops: the watchers the session started, and the tracked files you name with /projector <file>. It runs ps only to learn whether a hand-named file belongs to a review loop or a watch loop.

The change also turns each pull request's number from a Markdown link into a plain Button. Some terminals draw a link as its text followed by its URL, which pushed the row's state and title out of view, and a link takes no keyboard press on the main screen. As a button, the number opens its drawer with a click in fullscreen and with Enter on the main screen. Ctrl-click on the number, which opened the Projector summary directly, goes away; the drawer's projector link still opens it.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Band: the list Projector draws above the Claude Code prompt.
  • Loop: a review or fix loop whose watcher script polls GitHub for the pull requests in its tracked file.
  • Tracked file: the file a watcher's --tracked argument names, one owner/repo#number per line.
  • Kind: whether a loop is reviewing or watching, which the drawer shows.
  • Main screen: Claude Code's non-fullscreen layout, used under tmux, where the band takes key presses but no clicks.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The first Projector review of 5c1e142 found one open finding: the questions plan still compares its option numbers to a pull request's number as a Markdown link, which this change makes false. The flag on docs/projects/questions/readme.md below carries it.

groups.title: The band reads only the session's loops
groups.kicker: How the band finds its loops, and how a pull request's number is drawn
intro: The band keeps the loops it knows about in session state, the seenLoops atom. A loop enters that state in two ways: when the session runs a watcher through the Bash or Monitor tool, the hook records the watcher's tracked file and its kind; and when you run /projector <file>, the command records the file with no kind.

load used to merge that state with every watcher ps found on the machine. It now builds its list from the session state alone. It calls runningLoops, the function that runs ps, only when some recorded loop has no kind, and then only to look that kind up. A hand-named file whose watcher is not running falls back to watching, as before.

files.note: load drops the machine-wide watcher list; each pull request's number becomes a plain Button.

checks.text: own.every(...) is true for an empty list, so a session with no loops runs no ps either. Only a loop recorded by /projector <file> has no kind; adopt always records one.

Checked against the 2.1.296 claude-code.d.ts: Button takes plain and label, a plain Button draws its label alone, and a click or Enter under the focus raises onPress. tsc on hooks/ with those typings reports no errors.

groups.title: Tests for the session's own loops
groups.kicker: The band tests start each loop they expect to see
intro: The tests' shared world still runs a watch loop's watcher in another session, through its ps output. The first test now checks that the band leaves that loop out, asks GitHub only about the review loop's pull requests, and runs no ps. Tests that need both loops start the watch loop's watcher themselves through WATCH_COMMAND. The question tests' startSession now starts the review loop's watcher instead of running /projector, so the band still has a pull request to order the questions under.

files.note: Asserts the band ignores another session's watcher, presses the number as a Button, and adds a test for a hand-named file's kind.

groups.title: Documentation and plans
groups.kicker: The band's guide and two plans' open questions
intro: docs/plugins.md now says the band lists only this session's loops, that another session's loop stays out, and that you press ctrl+x tab and then Enter on a number to open a drawer on the main screen. The inbox plan (ready) and the questions plan (in-progress) each drop the open question about switching pull request numbers to buttons, which this change settles.
